almost 3.2 billion euros. Since 2022, figures have started to decrease again. Read more

payments.text:
Description: In the second quarter of 2024, eight percent of visits to e-commerce websites in Germany came from social media referrals. Tablets contributed the most, as 18 percent of their traffic to e-commerce sites came from social media links. Meanwhile, just
one percent of all desktop computer visits originated from social media. Read more
Note(s): Germany; Q2 2022 to Q2 2024
Source(s): Salesforce Research

29 Description: It is clear that both in-store and online shopping have different advantages. In Q4 2022, around 81 percent of respondents in Germany said that in terms of comparing prices and saving time, shopping online was better. In contrast, 71 percent of
respondents felt that shopping in-store led to better social interaction. Interestingly, although in many categories shopping online performs better, 60 percent of respondents still felt that the better overall shopping experience took place in-store. Read more
Note(s): Germany; Q4 2022; at least 1,000; 18 years and older
Source(s): Klarna; Nepa

Description: Looking at expected changes in online shopping behavior across Western Europe in 2023, consumers in the Netherlands were projected to spend a lot more in the next 12 months. More than half of Dutch respondents indicated their intention to
increase their online spending. In contrast, nearly a quarter of respondents in France and the UK said they intend to reduce e-spending. Read more
Note(s): Europe; July to August 2023; 5,000 online shoppers*; 18 years and older; expected change in the next 12 months; * The study was conducted across Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, and the UK. Around 1,000 surveys were [...] Read more

Description: In May 2025, mail order and online retail sales in Germany were 13.8 percent higher in real terms than in the same period of the previous year. In nominal terms, retail sales in the same month also increased, by 13.7 percent compared to the same
period in the previous year. The difference reflects the higher price level in the retail sector, although the upward price trend slowed significantly over the course of the past year. Read more
Note(s): Germany; preliminary figures
Source(s): Statistisches Bundesamt
